title: AO/394/2009 of THE NEW INDIA ASSURANCE COMPANY LTD Vs SMT. ANJU DEVI AND ORS

paras.text:
AO No. 394 of 2009
Honíble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
None
Mr. V.K. Kohli, Senior Advocate
assisted with Mr. I.P. Kohli, Advocate for
the appellant.
Learned Senior Counsel Mr. V.K.
Kohli, is present while none is present on
behalf of the respondents.
It is also pertinent to mention that
the learned counsel for the respondents
was not present yesterday and even
before on previous date so this Court,
looking to the factum that the accident is
of 2005 and the award was passed in
2009, is inclined to adjudicate this
appeal, which is pending since 2009
itself.
Young sole earning man of the
whole family lost his life in the accident
leaving completely blind father Shri Sher
Singh, mother Smt. Anju Devi and two
young sisters, as his dependents.
Learned Tribunal is granted an
award of Rs.5,70,000/- along with 6%
annual simple interest from the date of
institution of the petition.
Learned Senior Counsel of the
Insurance Company has challenged the
award, solely, on the ground that the
deceased was a youth, being unmarried,
hence one-third deduction towards
personal expenses, as has been held by
learned Tribunal, would have been one-half, as per Sarla Verma Case.
Considering the peculiar facts and
circumstances of the matter, this Court is
not inclined to accept such contention
because deceased youth was only hope of
his family and he was sole bread earner
of rest of four members of his family,
comprising blind father, mother and two
marriageable age young sisters.

It has been held by the Hon. Apex
Court time and again that in deciding the
quantum of award, there is no straight
jacket formula and amount of
compensation of sundry scores is subject
to variation considering the myriad
factors of the deceased family
 So, in view of what has been
highlighted above, I do not find any
cogent reasons to interfere with the
impugned judgment, therefore, dismiss
the appeal.
Rest of the amount, which is lying
in the learned Tribunal along with the
interest, earned during lying in the bank,
shall be disbursed to all the family
members as per their respective shares.
Remaining amount, if any, shall
also be returned to the Insurance
Company within six weeks from today.
Let a copy of this judgment along
with LCR be sent back to the Tribunal
concerned for information and
compliance.
 (Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.)
 27.09.2016
A.kaur
